title: Adaptive scan scheduler + tenant backpressure for long-run dashboard scrolls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Long dashboard scrolls and heavy exploratory queries from some tenants cause multi-minute tail latencies and IO spikes on the analytics read path. Current page-based pagination with fixed page size amplifies fan-out and produces hotspotting and large KV cache churn for larger windows.

Goal: Implement an adaptive scan scheduler that shapes scan work per-tenant based on run-time cost estimates, KV cache hit signals, and global load to reduce p99 tail latency and read amplification while maintaining median latency and throughput. Provide a tenant-level backpressure controller that can dynamically reduce per-tenant page sizes and throttle scan concurrency when system-wide SLOs are at risk.

Scope: backend query broker and scheduler only (no frontend changes). Deliverables include: a cost estimator module (heuristic based), a scheduling circuit that prioritizes small cheap scans and staggers heavy scans, per-tenant queue/shaper with token-bucket-like limits, and an operator-observable metric set and rollout plan.

Non-goals: full rewrite of index structures or storage layer. Not addressing write-side batching. No changes to authentication or RBAC in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler integrated into query-broker with toggle flag (feature-flagged rollout)
Observed p99 tail latency for dashboard scrolls reduced by at least 35% on 95th percentile tenants in the canary cluster
KV cache hit-stability measured (less than 10% extra evictions compared to baseline) during steady-state load
Per-tenant backpressure engages when cluster-wide load crosses configured SLO threshold and reduces median per-request token usage by at least 20%
Comprehensive metrics emitted (per-tenant scan cost estimate, scheduled start-delay, concurrency-limit, throttled-requests) and dashboards configured
Runbook updated with rollback steps and troubleshooting queries
comments: 2026-02-15 Asha Patel: Initial triage. Collected slow query traces and Grafana Dashboards showing repeated large-range scans from ~12 heavy tenants. Hypothesis: fixed page-size + parallel scan concurrency creates read amplification and eviction churn in shared KV cache.

2026-02-18 Miguel Torres: Design spike complete. Proposed components: cost-estimator (sample first N rows + histogram-based selectivity), scheduler that assigns a scheduled-start delay and 'scan-weight', and token-bucket per-tenant concurrency window. Draft architecture doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Adaptive+Scan+Scheduler

2026-02-22 Evelyn Wong (review): Recommended adding a fallback policy to avoid starvation of low-traffic tenants. Also suggested emitting a sampled detailed trace for any scan that gets delayed more than 500ms.

2026-02-28 Miguel Torres: Prototype implemented in query-broker branch (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4826). Feature-flag gate added: query.scheduler.adaptive_scan.enabled. Local microbench: mixed tenant workload, p99 down from 920ms -> 570ms (38% improvement) with 10% increase in median latency due to slight scheduling delay for large scans.

2026-03-04 Performance team: Canary run started in cluster canary-us-east-2. Initial telemetry looks promising but KV cache eviction rate increased by 8% during the first day; investigating mis-estimation of scan cost for sparse indexes.

2026-03-07 Miguel Torres: Fixed cost estimator to use bloom-filter sparsity and row-level tombstone density; eviction regression mitigated in follow-up commit (PR 4874). Added unit test coverage for cost estimator and deterministic scheduler fairness.

2026-03-10 PM review (Asha Patel): Approve canary expansion pending runbook and dashboards. Requested explicit backpressure thresholds exposed in Console for SRE config. Filed follow-up ENG-920102 for Console UI toggles.

2026-03-12 SRE notes: On canary cluster saw sustained p99 reduction across 80% of tenants. Noted two tenants where query patterns bypassed estimator (ad-hoc full-table exports); added an exclusion list feature that marks tenant queries as 'batch' to avoid scheduler and route them to a low-priority queue.
